newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Vestacor, M&A jump on rescue bid.
newsitem.headline: Vestacor, M&A jump on rescue bid.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Vestacor jumped 70 percent on Tuesday on speculation that a rescue bid by a consortium will revive its insolvent unit OfficeMart, analysts and dealers said on Tuesday.

A rescue bid for Vestacor, the pyramid holding firm for Mathieson & Ashley Holdings Ltd (M&A), whose main operating unit is OfficeMart, was been given the go-ahead by the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Friday.
An analyst who declined to be identified said the buying was mainly speculative at this stage.
"Vestacor was a cash shell before they took it over. It is a speculative buy at the moment, not investment quality," an analyst said.
Vestacor shares jumped by 28 cents to 68 cents in early trade but settled at 65 by 1140 GMT after 128,500 shares valued at more than 75,000 rand changed hands.
M&A gained 25 cents, or 55.6 percent, to a day high of 70 cents. Stocks were last at 65 cents in volume of 230,000 shares valued at nearly 142,000 rand.

Vestacor shares fell from 370 cents at the beginning of January to 43 cents on August 12, 1996 when the directors requested the JSE to suspended Vestacor and M$A shares pending clarity as to the future of the companies.
M$A shares fell from 351 cents in January 1995 to 20 cents on August 12, 1996.
OfficeMart went into provisional liquidation in August 1996 and had been insolvent since December, 1995.
The consortium has agreed to purchase outstanding claims against Vestacor and will subscribe for 120 million new Vestacor shares for five million rand cash.
It has also purchased all claims against M&A and will subscribe for 321.87 million M&A shares for a further five million rand cash.
Under the terms of the rescue bid the firms' listings will be suspended again should they not acquire viable assets within six months of relisting.
"Investors are perceiving it as a share to buy," a dealer said.
